title: quercus petraea subsp. iberica
intro: Quercus petraea subsp. iberica, commonly known as Iberian sessile oak, is a subspecies of the white oak tree native to the Iberian Peninsula. This plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health conditions due to its numerous health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Iberian sessile oak include wound healing, antiseptic, and antiviral activities, attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and tannins. The bioactive constituents of Quercus petraea subsp. iberica may also contribute to its potential in managing conditions like cardiovascular disease, diabetes, and cancer, although further research is needed to confirm these effects.
